summary: Per-route isolation mistakenly enabled for tenant uploader causing repeated 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed sustained 429 responses for a set of background uploader workers after enabling per-route isolation during an optimization rollout. Impact: uploader fleet from Parcellytics is seeing 20–30% of requests return 429s for periods of 30–90s, causing backfill lag and elevated retry traffic. The customer is on a Dedicated pool and rolled a config change from our console to enable per-route isolation to protect low-latency routes; they expected per-route buckets to be additive but are seeing tenant-wide exhaustion.

Observed behavior: After the config flip, multiple distinct routes used by the uploader ("/v1/generate", "/v1/embeddings") started receiving 429s concurrently. Headers in responses show x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and x-rate-limit-reset short windows (~5–8s) even though overall tenant token usage was below committed throughput.

Expected behavior: Per-route isolation should isolate heavy routes without starving other routes on the same tenant. For dedicated customers, enabling route isolation should maintain tenant-level capacity while enforcing per-route fairness, not cause cross-route token double-counting.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Dedicated tenant with multiple concurrently used routes (generate, embeddings, status checks).
2) From console, flip 'per_route_isolation' feature flag to true on dedicated pool config.
3) Start 50 parallel uploader workers that multiplex short-lived streams across routes with average request size ~200 tokens.
4) Observe burst period: many requests return 429 with response headers indicating depleted remaining tokens and rapid reset windows.
investigation_notes: 03/02 12:00 - Triage: Confirmed timing aligns with console change. No infra incidents in us-west during window per status page.

03/02 12:30 - Quota manager trace: per-route token buckets were created but configured with 'inherit_tenant_bucket=false' causing routes to draw from both route buckets and tenant bucket simultaneously due to an unintended dual-accounting codepath in the dedicated allocator.
03/03 09:15 - Reproduced in staging by enabling per_route_isolation; saw identical double-debit behavior when route buckets had low-burst and tenant bucket retention was not atomically transferred.

03/04 14:40 - Hypothesis: race in quota-manager during bucket creation for active flows causes temporary overlap where tokens are locked in both buckets for a short window; combined with short reset windows this manifests as quick 429 bursts even though net capacity exists.
comments: Support - Ana Torres (2026-03-02): Reached out to Parcellytics for request IDs and whether they used multiple API keys. Asked them to hold the console flag while we investigate.
Customer - Parcellytics (2026-03-02): Confirmed single API key; provided sample request IDs and said backfill latency climbed from 3h to 18h due to retries.
SRE - Marcus Lee (2026-03-03): Instrumented quota-manager to log bucket lifecycle events and correlated timestamp with 429 window; shared preliminary trace links in thread #support-dedicated.

Engineer - Daniel Wynn (2026-03-04): Identified codepath where allocateRouteBucket() calls createTenantBucketIfMissing() without an atomic transfer, introducing dual-accounting for 50-200ms on busiest routes. Preparing patch to make allocation atomic.
Support - Ana Torres (2026-03-05): Notified customer of workaround to temporarily disable per-route isolation and scheduled a short maintenance window to apply fix on their dedicated pool.
resolution: Workaround: Reverted per_route_isolation flag for Parcellytics at 2026-03-05 02:15 UTC which immediately eliminated 429 spikes. Permanent fix: Patch merged to quota-manager to make route bucket creation atomic and to ensure new route buckets are charged only from route OR tenant bucket (not both). Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/312. Rollout plan: staged to dedicated pools in us-west on 2026-03-06 with monitoring dashboards flagged. Follow-up: update docs to clarify expected semantics for per-route isolation and add console guardrail (warning when enabling on active uploaders).
